name: Alignment tax

subjectOf.text: Because institutional alignment emerges from architecture rather than from exogenous constraint, it scales with capability rather than against it: more capable agents accumulate deeper stakes, which strengthens rather than strains alignment.
subjectOf.abstract: Because this alignment emerges from institutional architecture rather than exogenous constraint, it scales with capability rather than against it. More capable agents accumulate deeper stakes, strengthening rather than straining alignment.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI's Mother's Instinct Engineered Consequence Emergent Ethics and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6244278
scope_conditions: alignment must be generated endogenously by institutional architecture
reputation must be accumulable by capability

subjectOf.text: Exogenous constraints scale against capability, since more powerful agents require more resources to constrain, producing an ever-increasing alignment tax.
subjectOf.abstract: Exogenous constraints scale against capability: the more powerful the agent, the greater the resources required to constrain it, producing an ever-increasing "alignment tax."
